Hi Claire —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our demo, I wanted to capture a concise implementation brief so we can lock the onboarding cadence and make the DB decision before next week's exec review. High-level asks:

- Confirm data volume (estimated docs / average size) and desired time-to-index for a backfill.
- Confirm latency SLO for top-k retrieval (p99 target) and any hard budget constraints.
- Decide whether SearchLytics prefers a managed vector DB (Pinecone / FAISS managed service) versus self-hosted (Milvus on EKS / pgvector).
- Provide an initial sample corpus (5–10k records) for our rerank smoke tests and evaluation.

I attached the technical requirements workbook (searchlytics-technical-requirements.xlsx) we discussed — please drop in the volume estimates tab if convenient.

Proposed cadence (high level):
1) Week 0: Preflight — sample ingestion, environment validation, small-seed rerank eval
2) Weeks 1–2: Seed index (0.5–1M) + rerank A/B smoke test
3) Weeks 3–6: Parallel backfill + monitor + incremental quality gates

If you and Matt are aligned, we can put Marissa and Monica on a concrete task list tomorrow to produce an ops checklist and DB recommendation by EOD Monday.

Best,

Jordan — thanks for the write-up. Quick clarifications from our side:

- Volume: ~120M documents; average doc size ~2.5KB (we'll upload the detailed breakdown).
- Latency SLO: p95 < 120ms for retrieval+rerank within our UI; p99 preferred < 300ms.
- Data residency: must remain in AWS us-east-1 for compliance with our EU data flow policy.
- Budget: initial pilot budgeted up to $25k/mo for hosted infra, but long-term we need an ops-friendly model under $12k/mo.

We can share a 10k sample set by EOD. Attaching a CSV with our volume estimates (volume_estimates.csv).

On DB preference: at this scale our infra team leans toward a managed service for the pilot (Pinecone or managed Milvus) to reduce ops burden, but we will evaluate cost tradeoffs vs self-hosted in production.

Matt will loop his infra lead if we go self-hosted. Happy to proceed with your proposed cadence — please include a short risk matrix for backfill (throttling, bad payloads, deduping).

Thanks — I pulled the sample and the CSV. Draft plan below (summary):

Executive recommendation (pilot): use managed Milvus (EKS-based managed offering) or Pinecone for the pilot to minimize ops overhead. If SearchLytics needs sub-$12k/mo production, plan a 2-phase migration: pilot on managed, production on optimized self-hosted infra with tuned quantization and tiered cold storage.

Phased cadence (6 weeks) — owners in parens:
- Week 0: Preflight (Marissa)
  - Ingest 10k sample; validate schema and dedupe rules
  - Smoke retrieval & rerank using Redwood's small-seed flow
- Weeks 1–2: Seed index (Monica / Infra contact)
  - Seed 0.5–1M docs; validate latency & storage metrics; cost run-rate estimate
- Weeks 3–4: Incremental backfill + monitoring (Monica)
  - Backfill at controlled throughput; use KV/prefix caching where possible; snapshot checkpoints every 50M docs
- Weeks 5–6: Rerank A/B + acceptance (Jordan / Marissa)
  - Pairwise A/B on critical queries; evaluate against acceptance criteria below

Acceptance criteria (short):
- Retrieval p95 <= 120ms on us-east-1 test cluster for seeded index
- Rerank model improves top-3 precision by >= 8% vs baseline on acceptance prompt set
- No critical errors or backfill failures for 48h at target throughput

Ops pros/cons (short):
- Managed Milvus / Pinecone: fast time-to-pilot, SLA-backed, limited infra ops; higher monthly cost for large scale
- Self-hosted Milvus / pgvector: lower unit cost at scale, more control (zone affinity), higher engineering ops burden

Risks & mitigations:
- Throttling: implement producer-side rate limiter and backfill checkpointing
- Bad payloads: small preflight validation and quarantining of malformed records
- Schema drift: enforce column/field contracts and incremental validation jobs

I'll attach the cadence doc and an ops checklist (implementation_cadence_v1.pdf). Monica — can you add the backfill runbook items and a checklist for checkpointing?

— Marissa

Looping Claire in with the ops checklist and explicit runbook steps. I created a lightweight backfill checklist and a rerank eval template for immediate use. Key runbook excerpts below:

Backfill runbook (excerpts):
- Preflight: validate sample ingestion schema, confirm field mapping and tokenization settings (owner: SearchLytics infra).
- Throttled backfill: start at 100 docs/sec, increase by 2x every 12h while monitoring p95 retrieval latency and CPU/GPU utilization. Backfill pause threshold: if p95 retrieval > 300ms for 30m, rollback to previous checkpoint.
- Checkpointing: create snapshots every 50M docs (S3 prefix: s3://searchlytics-backfills/checkpoints/). Maintain manifest file with checksum and row counts.
- Dedup & normalization: run dedupe job pre-ingest (hash + heuristic) and quarantined records to a quarantine bucket for manual review.

Rerank eval template & acceptance:
- Use provided 10k sample to generate 1k evaluation queries; evaluate baseline vs rerank model by top-3 precision and MRR.
- Threshold: +8% top-3 precision OR +0.04 MRR to pass; failure requires rollback to canary index and 72h hold.

Immediate asks from SearchLytics to unblock Monday:
1) SSO contact & admin invite (for Console)
2) Pilot AWS account number (us-east-1) and IAM role with S3 read access
3) Confirmation on managed vs self-hosted for pilot (we will proceed with managed by default if no reply by Tue EOD)
